name: Castorides
description:
Castoroides, also known as the giant beaver, was a massive rodent that lived during the Pleistocene epoch, around 2.5 million to 10,000 years ago in North America. It could grow up to 8 feet (2.5 meters) long and weigh over 200 pounds, making it the largest beaver species that ever lived. Unlike modern beavers, Castoroides had massive incisors shaped more for slicing than gnawing, and there’s no solid evidence that it built dams or lodges. It likely lived in wetlands, feeding on aquatic plants and shrubs.

Castoroides coexisted with other Ice Age megafauna such as mammoths, dire wolves, and saber-toothed cats. Its fossils are often found near ancient lakes and rivers, painting a picture of a giant, semi-aquatic herbivore that played a vital role in its ecosystem before going extinct at the end of the last Ice Age.

name: Leaellynasaura sp. Reconstruction & Animation
description:
An Australian dinosaur walks again?! ***Leaellynasaura amicagraphica*** ('*Leaellyn's friend writing lizard*') was a small herbivorous ornithopod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Victoria, Australia (**122.46 - 109 million years ago**). They lived in a polar Australia that was much further south on the globe, dealt with darkness that would last for months, and had a remarkably long tail (**>90 verts**).

This 3D skeletal reconstruction was created by [Astrid O’Connor](https://www.instagram.com/palaeoastrid/) in Blender (v3.4) as a tool for the **Dinosaur Dreaming** team to utilise for science communication. Astrid utilised a novel morphing method to reconstruct some of the missing axial bones.

The vast majority of this model was based on the osteology of ***Hypsilophodon foxii***, 3D models of the ***Leaellynasaura*** holoytype, and reconstructions  created by **Alana Sharp**. This reconstruction was advised by **Ruairidh Duncan** and the creator thanks **Tom Rich** and **Patricia Vickers-Rich**.

-Hand-painted scars, wet-skin detailing & mouth cavity realism

-Fully compatible with all PBR workflows

**Uses**

Perfect for creature design, cinematics, horror environments, deep-sea scenes, concept art, VFX, or storytelling projects.

**Made With:**

-Blender (modeling, rigging, animating)

-Substance 3D Painter (texturing)

name: Snail Matchbox (NHMW-ZOO-MO-0081100-ETH-055)
description:
3d scan of a matchbox shaped like a little land snail which is part of the Uetz collection.

Karl Uetz (1914–1998) was a private collector and owner of a large mollusc collection. In addition to thousands of snail and mussel shells, the collection also contains approximately 200 art and everyday objects as well as ethnographic objects. The collection was purchased by the NHMW in 1974 and digitised in 2025.

**Object**: Zündholzbehälter in Schneckenform

**Inventory number**: NHMW-ZOO-MO-0081100-ETH-055

**Collection**: NHMW, 3rd Zoological Dept., Collection Mollusca (curator: Anita Eschner)

Find out more about the NHMW [here](http://www.nhm.at/en).

Text by A. Eschner

Scanned & edited by A. Haider (NHMW)
